title: Work as worship
hook: kirat, honest labor, is itself devotion

segments.voice: Yesterday, grihasth, the householder's path: the lotus in the pond, spotless in the soot. Your line was holiness at home. Which ordinary moment at home did you treat as part of the path? Day one thousand three hundred eighty.

Two invitations to dinner arrive on the same evening. One comes from a carpenter named Lalo, a poor man who works with his hands. His table has coarse bread. The other comes from Malik Bhago, a rich official, who is throwing a grand feast and expects the holy man in town to attend. The janamsakhis, the old stories of Guru Nanak's life, say the Guru stayed with Lalo and didn't go to the feast. Bhago was offended, and demanded to know why. What the stories say happened next is a scene Sikhs still retell, and it is today's lesson.
screen: `TWO DINNER INVITATIONS.` → `A CARPENTER'S BREAD. A RICH MAN'S FEAST.` → `THE GURU STAYS WITH LALO.`

segments.voice: First, the story's answer. The tradition says Guru Nanak took a piece of Lalo's coarse bread in one hand and a piece of Bhago's rich food in the other, and squeezed. From Lalo's bread came milk. From Bhago's came blood. The point lands without a speech: one meal was earned by honest hands; the other was squeezed out of other people. Second, the word. Kirat is honest work, earning a living by your own effort without cheating anyone. We met it earlier in this part of the year, beside the farmer who can't make it rain, named alongside remembering the Name and sharing. Today it gets a story of its own. Third, what the Granth says. In a salok, Guru Nanak puts it in a line. In paraphrase: the one who eats what they have earned by their own work, and gives some of it from their hand, Nanak, that one recognizes the path. Notice the order. First the earning. The path is recognized in the work, not only in the temple. Fourth, why work can be worship. If freedom can come while laughing and eating, as Guru Arjan said three days ago, it can come at a workbench too. Fixing a sink, teaching a class, stocking shelves, driving a delivery route, caring for a patient at night: done honestly, each is a kind of devotion. Not because the job is holy in itself, but because honesty in it is a way of remembering the One. Lalo's bread was ordinary. What made it sweet was how it was earned. Work is worship.
screen: `LALO'S BREAD AND BHAGO'S FEAST.` · `KIRAT: HONEST WORK.` · `EAT WHAT YOU EARN, GIVE FROM YOUR HAND.` · `THE WORKBENCH AS A PLACE OF PRAYER.` · then, large: `WORK IS WORSHIP.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: work honestly today. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the next piece of work in front of you, paid or unpaid: a report, a shift, homework, laundry, a repair. Picture yourself doing it all the way through without a single shortcut you'd be embarrassed to explain. No padding the hours, no blaming someone else, no cutting the corner nobody would see. Notice how that feels in the body. Then just breathe with it. If you pray, you can offer the work with Waheguru before you begin. The bell holds the time.
Work as worship. Kirat, honest work, earned by your own effort, which Sikh teaching treats as devotion itself. Today's word.
Your line: work is worship. Today, choose one task and do it the way Lalo earned his bread: plainly, honestly, all the way through. Day one thousand three hundred eighty.

howItsDone: Sikhs speak of kirat karni, earning an honest living by one's own work, as part of the path alongside remembering the Name and sharing, and tell the story of Bhai Lalo and Malik Bhago to show it.

fork.setup: you're a traveling teacher, and both a poor carpenter and a rich official invite you to dinner the same night. what do you do?
options: go to the rich man's feast; he can help many people.
stay with the carpenter and eat his coarse bread.
fork.reveal: the janamsakhis say Guru Nanak stayed with Lalo, and when Bhago demanded why, squeezed milk from Lalo's bread and blood from Bhago's food.

trapdoor: what you thought: worship happens in the gurdwara, and work is what you do to pay the bills.
what it means: honest work, kirat, is itself devotion.
what a scholar hears: Guru Nanak's salok: one who eats what they earn and gives from their hand recognizes the path.

notes: Editor: kirat is now named as a callback to day 1366 (kirat karo beside the farmer) rather than introduced again; 'the Guru is found while laughing and eating' corrected to what day 1377's Gujri ki Var line says (liberation, not the Guru) and 'this week' fixed (1377 was the previous week); 'Lalo baked his bread' changed to 'earned' (he was a carpenter).
Paraphrase of 'ghaal khaae kichh hathhu dei, Nanak raahu pachhaanahi sei' (Ang 1245); please confirm the Ang and that it is a salok of Guru Nanak in Sarang ki Var.
The Lalo and Bhago story is told as janamsakhi tradition; no place name is given. Please confirm details (Lalo a carpenter, Bhago an official, milk and blood).
'Sikhs speak of kirat karni ... alongside remembering the Name and sharing' presents the three together without a count; please confirm the framing.
Tomorrow (1381) also leans on the second half of the Ang 1245 line (giving from your hand); today only names it.
